item.title: Total endovascular arch repair: should it be the first-line option in the elective treatment of aortic arch aneurysms?
item.description: BACKGROUND: Although the traditional standard of care for aortic arch aneurysms is open surgical arch replacement, this approach usually requires sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass and hypothermic arrest. Even among the subset of patients fit for open surgery, it is associated with a pooled mortality and stroke rate of around 5%. item.title: Overcoming hostile neck anatomy in endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm repair using the reverse slider technique – a case report
item.description: Background: Around 40-60% of abdominal aorta aneurysm (AAA) patients are deemed to be outside the instructions for use (IFU) for endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) because of hostile anatomy. Short and angulated necks pose a serious risk of type IA endoleak due to the difficulty in achieving proper proximal fixation and endograft seal. item.title: Popliteal artery entrapment syndrome: a case report and review of the literature
item.description: BACKGROUND: Popliteal Artery Entrapment Syndrome (PAES) is an uncommon but important cause of lower limb ischemia affecting young, active individuals without traditional atherosclerotic risk factors. The condition has an estimated prevalence of 0.17–3.5% in the general population and accounts for approximately 3–5% of claudication cases in patients under 40 years without atherosclerotic risk factors. item.title: Spinal cord ischaemia predictors and outcomes in complex endovascular aortic repair – a single centre retrospective study
item.description: Introduction Spinal cord ischemia (SCI) is an infrequent distressing complication following thoraco-abdominal (TAAA) and complex abdominal aortic aneurysm (CAAA) repair. Prior studies showed controversial results regarding risk factors and preventive measures. item.title: The impact of subintimal lesion crossing on femoro-popliteal endovascular treatment outcomes
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Subintimal angioplasty is an endovascular technique used to recanalize occluded segments in the arterial bed that cannot be crossed via an intraluminal path. However, there is still limited data regarding the clinical outcome of subintimal angioplasty. The aim of this study is to evaluate the impact of subintimal angioplasty in femoro-popliteal lesions.
